purpose: Extensible lexicon of religions, traditions, denominations and nonreligious worldviews with concise descriptive definitions.
method: Traditions are separated from denominations and political movements. Definitions are descriptive rather than theological judgments. Religious classification should preserve internal diversity.
entries: christianity
Religion centered on Jesus Christ, his teachings, death and resurrection; encompassing many churches and traditions.
catholicism
Christian tradition centered on communion with the Bishop of Rome and the Catholic Church's sacramental and teaching tradition.
eastern-orthodoxy
Christian communion of churches emphasizing ancient liturgy, apostolic succession, councils and Orthodox theology.
oriental-orthodoxy
Family of ancient Christian churches including Coptic, Armenian, Syriac, Ethiopian and Eritrean traditions.
protestantism
Family of Christian traditions originating in the Reformation and emphasizing reform of Western Christianity.
anglicanism
Christian tradition originating in the Church of England, combining Protestant and catholic elements.
lutheranism
Protestant tradition originating with Martin Luther and emphasizing justification by faith and scripture.
calvinism
Reformed Protestant tradition associated with John Calvin and Reformed theology.
presbyterianism
Reformed Protestant family characterized by government through elders and presbyteries.
baptists
Protestant traditions emphasizing believer's baptism, congregational life and religious liberty.
methodism
Protestant tradition emerging from the Wesleyan revival and emphasizing disciplined Christian life and grace.
pentecostalism
Christian movement emphasizing the experiential work of the Holy Spirit, including spiritual gifts.
evangelicalism
Cross-denominational Christian movement emphasizing conversion, biblical authority and evangelism.
adventism
Christian family emphasizing the Second Coming and distinctive eschatological teaching.
mormonism
Restorationist Christian movement centered on the Book of Mormon and the teachings of Joseph Smith; commonly associated with the Latter-day Saint movement.
jehovahs-witnesses
Christian-derived restorationist movement emphasizing Jehovah, evangelism and distinctive biblical interpretation.
islam
Monotheistic Abrahamic religion centered on the Qur'an and the prophetic example of Muhammad.
sunni-islam
Largest Islamic tradition, recognizing the authority of the Sunnah and a broad inherited scholarly tradition.
shia-islam
Islamic tradition emphasizing the religious authority and succession of the Prophet's family, especially the Imams.
ibadi-islam
Early Islamic tradition distinct from Sunni and Shia traditions, historically prominent in Oman and parts of North Africa.
sufism
Mystical and devotional currents within Islam emphasizing spiritual purification and experiential knowledge of God.
ahmadiyya
Islamic movement founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in nineteenth-century India, with distinctive beliefs about messianic fulfillment.
judaism
Abrahamic religion and civilization centered on covenant, Torah, Jewish law, interpretation and communal tradition.
orthodox-judaism
Jewish tradition emphasizing binding observance of halakha and continuity with rabbinic law and tradition.
conservative-judaism
Modern Jewish movement balancing commitment to Jewish law with historical development and modern scholarship.
reform-judaism
Jewish movement emphasizing evolving tradition, ethical principles and individual or communal interpretation of Jewish law.
reconstructionist-judaism
Jewish movement understanding Judaism as an evolving religious civilization and emphasizing democratic communal practice.
hinduism
Family of South Asian religious traditions involving diverse philosophies, practices, deities and concepts of dharma and liberation.
vaishnavism
Hindu traditions centered devotionally on Vishnu and his avatars, especially Krishna and Rama.
shaivism
Hindu traditions centered on Shiva and diverse Shaiva theological and devotional systems.
shaktism
Hindu traditions centered on the divine feminine or Shakti as ultimate or central sacred power.
smartism
Hindu tradition associated with Advaita Vedanta and worship of multiple major deities as manifestations of one ultimate reality.
buddhism
Religious-philosophical traditions derived from the Buddha's teachings concerning suffering, liberation, karma and awakening.
theravada-buddhism
Buddhist tradition prominent in Sri Lanka and mainland Southeast Asia, emphasizing the Pali canon and monastic path.
mahayana-buddhism
Broad Buddhist family emphasizing bodhisattva ideals and a large body of later scriptures and philosophical traditions.
vajrayana-buddhism
Tantric Buddhist traditions using ritual, visualization, mantra and other esoteric practices, especially in Himalayan and related traditions.
sikhism
Monotheistic South Asian religion founded in the teachings of the Sikh Gurus and centered on the Guru Granth Sahib.
jainism
Ancient Indian religion emphasizing nonviolence, disciplined conduct, karma and liberation of the soul.
zoroastrianism
Ancient Iranian religious tradition associated with Zarathustra and centered on ethical choice, truth and devotion to Ahura Mazda.
bahai-faith
Global religion founded by Baha'u'llah emphasizing unity of humanity, progressive revelation and global peace.
yazidism
Enduring religious tradition of the Yazidi people with its own sacred narratives, rituals and communal institutions.
druze-faith
Esoteric monotheistic tradition historically emerging in the Ismaili Shi'a environment and developing a distinct communal identity.
mandaeanism
Gnostic religious tradition centered on John the Baptist, ritual immersion and distinctive cosmology.
samaritanism
Ancient Israelite religious tradition of the Samaritan community centered on the Torah and Mount Gerizim.
rastafari
Jamaican religious movement combining biblical themes, African identity, Ethiopia-centered symbolism and resistance to oppression.
african-traditional-religions
Diverse indigenous African religious systems involving ancestors, spirits, ritual specialists, cosmology and community obligations.
yoruba-religion
West African religious tradition involving Olodumare, orishas, divination, ritual and ancestral relationships.
vodou
Religious tradition of Haiti and related communities combining West African, Catholic and local Caribbean elements.
santeria
Afro-Cuban religious tradition combining Yoruba-derived orisha devotion with Catholic forms and Cuban cultural history.
candomble
Brazilian Afro-diasporic religious tradition centered on orixás, ritual communities, possession and African-derived practice.
traditional-chinese-religion
Plural Chinese religious complex involving ancestor veneration, local deities, ritual, divination and overlapping Daoist and Confucian elements.
taoism
Chinese religious-philosophical tradition associated with Daoist texts, cultivation, ritual, cosmology and harmony with the Dao.
confucianism
Chinese ethical and philosophical tradition centered on moral cultivation, social roles, learning, ritual and humane governance.
shinto
Japanese religious tradition involving kami, ritual purity, shrine practice and relationships between community, place and sacred presence.
tenrikyo
Japanese new religious tradition founded by Nakayama Miki emphasizing joyful life and divine parenthood.
caodaism
Vietnamese syncretic religion combining elements from East Asian and Western religious traditions.
hoa-hao
Vietnamese Buddhist-derived religious movement emphasizing simplified practice and ethical living.
new-religious-movements
Umbrella category for newer religious movements arising outside or alongside established traditions.
neopaganism
Family of modern movements inspired by pre-Christian European and other historical pagan traditions.
wicca
Modern pagan religious tradition involving ritual magic, seasonal observances and reverence for divine polarity or nature.
druidry
Modern religious and spiritual movement inspired by ancient Celtic traditions, nature reverence and poetic or ritual practice.
animism
Broad religious orientation treating animals, plants, places, objects or natural phenomena as possessing spirit or agency.
shamanism
Umbrella term for traditions involving specialist mediation with spirits or other-than-human realms through ritual practice.
atheism
Position of lacking belief in gods or affirming that gods do not exist; it includes several philosophical forms.
agnosticism
Position that knowledge of whether gods or the supernatural exist is unavailable, uncertain or not currently justified.
secular-humanism
Nonreligious worldview emphasizing human dignity, reason, ethics and human flourishing without requiring supernatural belief.
deism
Theological position affirming a creator or first cause while generally rejecting ongoing revealed intervention.
pantheism
View identifying God or divinity with the universe or totality of reality.
panentheism
View that the universe exists within God while God is understood as more than the universe.
polytheism
Religious worldview recognizing multiple gods or divine beings.
monotheism
Religious worldview affirming one God as ultimate deity.
henotheism
Religious pattern involving devotion to one deity without necessarily denying the existence of others.
animistic-indigenous-worldviews
Plural category for indigenous traditions in which land, ancestors, animals, spirits and community are integrated in religious life.
atheist-humanism
Humanist outlook explicitly grounded in nonbelief in gods while retaining secular ethical commitments.
spiritual-but-not-religious
Contemporary identity describing spiritual or transcendent commitments without formal affiliation to an organized religion.
esotericism
Family of traditions emphasizing hidden, initiatory or symbolic knowledge and spiritual transformation.
gnosticism
Family of ancient and modern movements emphasizing saving knowledge or direct spiritual insight, with varied cosmologies.
mysticism
Religious orientation emphasizing direct experiential encounter with ultimate reality or the divine.
syncretism
Combination or mutual adaptation of elements from multiple religious traditions.
folk-religion
Lived religious practice combining formal traditions with local customs, ancestors, spirits, festivals and popular devotion.
source_framework: The World Religion Database distinguishes major religions, second-level traditions and detailed denominational or local categories; this atlas follows that layered principle rather than pretending every tradition is a single homogeneous block.
